title: Chemical compatibility and SDS decision exercises
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain hazards and scope boundaries for chemical compatibility
Demonstrate an authorised procedure with appropriate controls

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Identify the actual task
instruction.body: Start with the soil, surface, people present and intended outcome. A disinfectant is not automatically needed for every cleaning task. Check the work order, product label, manufacturer surface guidance and site procedures before choosing a product.

instruction.heading: Read the SDS alongside the label
instruction.body: Find hazard identification, safe handling, exposure controls, first aid, accidental release, storage and incompatibility information. The SDS informs risk assessment; the current product label gives specific use instructions. If documents conflict or are unavailable, stop and ask the supervisor.

instruction.heading: Test the compatibility decision
instruction.body: Compare the proposed product against the surface and existing residues. Acidic descalers may damage acid-sensitive stone; oxidisers may affect some finishes. Never mix products, including bleach with acids or ammonia-containing products. Do not infer compatibility from colour, fragrance or marketing terms.

instruction.heading: Choose a safer response
instruction.body: For an unknown residue or unlabelled container, isolate it from use and escalate. Never sniff, taste or experimentally combine chemicals. For a sensitive finish, use the authorised alternative or request specialist guidance.

instruction.heading: Document the decision
instruction.body: Record the task, product name, relevant label directions, surface, PPE/ventilation requirements, identified hazards, selected controls and any stop-work escalation. A supervisor reviews decisions before independent use.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Identify the task first: note the soil, the surface, the people present and the outcome needed, before choosing any product.
Check the work order, the current product label, the manufacturer's surface guidance and the site procedure, and follow the label directions for use.
Read the safety data sheet (SDS) alongside the label, noting hazard identification, safe handling, exposure controls, first aid, storage and incompatibility.
Test the proposed product against the surface and any existing residue, and never mix products, including bleach with acids or ammonia-containing products.
Do not infer compatibility from colour, fragrance or marketing terms; use the authorised alternative for a sensitive finish.
For an unknown residue or unlabelled container, isolate it from use and escalate; never sniff, taste or experiment with it.
If the SDS and the label conflict or are unavailable, stop and ask the supervisor before proceeding.

Record the task, product name, label directions, surface, PPE and ventilation, identified hazards, selected controls and any stop-work escalation, and have a supervisor review the decision before independent use.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: The proposed product is checked against the surface, the label and the site procedure before use.
The SDS hazard, handling, first aid, storage and incompatibility sections are read alongside the label.
No products are mixed, and compatibility is never inferred from colour, fragrance or marketing terms.
Each decision records the product, label directions, PPE and ventilation, hazards and selected controls.
summary: A disinfectant is not needed for every task, so the cleaner checks the work order, the product label, the surface guidance and the site procedure before choosing a product.
The SDS informs the risk assessment and the current label gives the specific use directions, and missing or conflicting documents mean stopping to ask.
Products are never mixed, and an unknown residue is isolated and escalated.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen when the correct method or authorisation is uncertain?
options: The worker uses the product that looks most suitable for the job at hand today
The worker stops, isolates the product and asks the supervisor before using it
The worker mixes two products to test which one works best on the job today
The worker uses the strongest product and reports it afterwards

knowledgeChecks.question: What evidence demonstrates completion of this task?
options: A statement that the worker read the label on the product, the box, the sheet, the cart and the tray
The empty product bottle kept on the cart for the record, the day, the shift, the job and the bin
A decision record with the product name, label directions, surface, PPE, hazards and controls
A photo of the product on the shelf in the store, the van, the depot, the cart and the bin

knowledgeChecks.question: How should an out-of-scope request be handled?
options: Accept it, because the product is already on the shelf
Do it quickly and report it later to the team and the supervisor
Ask a colleague to do it without telling the supervisor
Decline the request or refer it, and record it for the supervisor
